defect.snippet: for (let i = 0; i < SALT_BUCKETS - 1; i++) keys.push(viewKey(videoId, i));

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code reads or writes the partitioned counter keys? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: record() writes to buckets 0..15 (hash % SALT_BUCKETS), but total() only reads buckets 0..14 because the loop stops at SALT_BUCKETS - 1. Views landing in bucket 15 (about 1/16 of sessions) are never counted, so every video under-reports by roughly 6%.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does the key format wrap the video id in braces, as in views:{abc}:3?
choices: Braces are required by Redis for numeric values
It makes keys sort by bucket number
In Redis Cluster the hash tag forces all buckets of one video into the same slot, so MGET and DEL across them work
It prevents key collisions between videos with similar ids
choiceQuestions.explanation: Redis Cluster hashes only the substring inside {} when present, so all bucket keys of a video share a slot and multi-key commands like MGET/DEL are allowed. Braces have nothing to do with value types or sort order, and the colon-separated prefix already distinguishes videos.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Given that hash tag, what does salting the key into 16 buckets actually achieve for a viral video?
choices: It spreads write load across 16 cluster nodes
It reduces contention on a single key but all buckets still live on one node, so node-level hot spotting remains
It makes total() eventually consistent across replicas
It guarantees each viewer is counted only once
choiceQuestions.explanation: Because every bucket shares one hash tag, they map to one slot and one node; salting splits the single hot key into 16 keys but does not spread load across nodes. It has no effect on replica consistency, and nothing deduplicates viewers: the same session simply increments the same bucket again.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Redis is briefly unreachable. What do clients see when posting a view?
choices: A 202, with the view silently lost and a warning logged
A 400 because the session header is rejected
The request hangs until Redis recovers
choiceQuestions.explanation: The POST handler catches errors from record(), logs a warning, and still responds 202, so the view is dropped. It does not call next(err), so no 500; the 400 path is only for a missing header; and the catch path responds immediately after the failed call.
